labels.why: Choosing the invoking surface and its context is how the bot meets the existing org.
A sharing-context rule; it is a security boundary of the bot itself.
Honouring field-level security is a security rule the bot must follow.
An access control via permission sets; security rigour for the bot.
A privacy rule on conversations; security rigour.
An async design decision forced by the real runtime's callout rules.
Where the credential is kept; security rigour.
Governor limits have to be stated with their numbers; these are platform quotas.
The test approach against the real runtime's constraints.
A deployment step without which the callout is refused.
The flow by which the interface gets the async answer; part of the core behaviour.
An idempotency rule for retried jobs; failure-handling rigour.
Queue and concurrency caps, plus what happens past them; quota rigour.
Names the failure classes (4xx, 5xx, timeout) that each get their own outcome; this is error behaviour.
A backoff and retry policy for provider quota; quota and failure rigour.
What the user sees for partial or missing answers; the bot's own error behaviour.
The record shape the async request and reply must live in; usage counts serve quota tracking.
Retention and deletion of stored conversations; data-retention rigour.
A rule on what goes into the prompt; a security and personal-data boundary.
The context-window size at which history is trimmed; a boundary of the bot's behaviour.
Edge cases treated apart (no history, empty question) plus a maximum length; the bot's boundaries.
Seeing failed requests is failure routing (needed); the off switch and model switching are admin controls (beyond).
A separate audit store of questions and answers; the bot works without it.
Per-environment configuration and deployment steps; deployment rigour. The coverage figure is mentioned only in passing.
A latency bound plus truthful progress feedback while the async answer is pending.
Names the interface states (empty, loading, error, refused) the bot's UI must handle.
Existing org behaviour must be preserved.
The core promotion behaviour (automatic or offer); the window only matters if an offer is chosen.
Join-time order and tie-breaking are needed; tier or staff priority that jumps the queue is a further feature (beyond).
A resolution rule for overlapping waitlists; promotion is wrong without it.
How the waitlist meets the existing no-show policy.
The background trigger for promotion; part of how the feature works.
A promoted person has to be told, and send failures have to be handled; core behaviour plus failure handling.
A concurrency rule that prevents double promotion and overbooking.
A race between direct booking and promotion; correctness of the feature.
How promotion meets existing payment, including its failure.
A waitlist cap and the behaviour at it; a boundary of the feature.
A time cut-off for promotion; a boundary of the feature.
How existing capacity editing interacts with the waitlist.
What happens to waiters when the class is cancelled; it meets existing behaviour.
The waitlist entry record the feature depends on.
Retention of waitlist entries; data-retention rigour.
A member seeing their own waitlist state while other people's identities stay private; core behaviour plus privacy.
A staff view, manual promote and remove, and promotion history are further controls the waitlist works without.
Feature toggles per class or class type are a further control.
A timeliness bound on promotion; a boundary of the core behaviour.
Existing booking behaviour must be preserved.
A rollout decision for classes already full; how the feature meets existing data.
A reminder count and time offsets have to be stated; this is the core schedule.
Names the invoice states that stop the sequence.
A content rule for part-paid invoices; the reminder is wrong without it.
Names the existing customer contact states that suppress reminders, and the exemption.
An idempotency rule; failure and deployment rigour.
A send-time check that prevents reminders on invoices already paid.
A retry policy and escalation; failure routing and ownership.
The provider rate limit and pacing within it; quota rigour.
Rollout behaviour for the existing overdue backlog; the switch-on would be wrong without it.
Local time and sending hours are needed (a bound plus excluded days); a holiday calendar is a further store (beyond).
Formatting of the amount in the reminder; correctness of its content.
Error behaviour for a bad recipient or no contact at all.
A decision on which contact receives the reminder; core behaviour.
A send record per step is needed for idempotency and tracing; showing it on the invoice is a further view (beyond).
What the reminder says; the requested outcome's own content.
Authority over the schedule configuration is needed security; manual send and stop are further controls (beyond).
Off switches, preview or dry-run, and manual resend are further controls.
Visibility of failed sends is failure routing (needed); a view of upcoming sends is a further view (beyond).
A bound on volume or lateness; quota and timeliness rigour.
Existing invoice behaviour must be preserved.
A partial-failure decision; core error behaviour.
The import result naming failed rows; core error behaviour.
A decision on existing and duplicate rows; the import is wrong without it.
A privilege-escalation check; security rigour.
Access control on importing; security rigour.
The required and accepted columns and the header cases have to be named; file validation.
Names the encoding and shape variants the parser must accept.
Behaviour when a failure follows side effects; core error behaviour.
A size or row cap, and the behaviour above it.
Edge-case files treated apart: empty, header-only, single row.
An idempotency rule for re-uploads.
Background processing and the admin learning of completion; how the import works on the real runtime.
A pacing rate for invitation mail; quota rigour.
The initial state of a created user; the requested outcome's own behaviour.
Storage, retention and access of the uploaded personal data; retention and security rigour.
Parsing rules for values; correctness of the import.
A separate audit record the import works without.
Cancel and retry-failed-rows are further controls.
A duration bound for a maximum-size file, with progress shown while it runs.
Existing user creation and existing users must be preserved.
Defence against formula injection and overlong fields; security rigour.
